messages.subject: Whitcombe - first read on the file
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

Having been through the consultation bundle, my initial view:

- The redundancy rationale (loss of the Halcyon ambient contract, throughput down ~28% at Coleshill) is well evidenced. That helps a lot on the s.98 case.
- The selection scoring is the weak point. Whitcombe scored 41 vs Driscoll's 47, but two of the criteria are quite subjective and Tennant scored both. Given Tennant is also the disclosure recipient, the claimant will hammer the conflict.
- On s.103A, the timing (disclosure 9 Sep, consultation 1 Dec) is uncomfortably tight. I'd put us at around 60-65% on defeating the automatic unfair limb.

I think we file a robust ET3 but advise the client early that this is a sensible one to settle. Drafting the grounds now.

Best wishes,
Tom Gallagher
Associate | Employment
Whitfield Carter LLP
T +44 (0)20 7946 0538

Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Whitcombe - first read on the file
messages.plaintextBody:
Agreed on all counts. Build the redundancy/throughput evidence prominently in the grounds, and let's be careful not to overstate the maintenance investigation - we want to show the concerns were dealt with, not that they were buried. Put a merits/quantum note together for the client for the week of the 21st; flag the uncapped tail risk clearly. SW

Kind regards,
Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Employment & Dispute Resolution
Whitfield Carter LLP
